name: Ivan Kotliarevsky
credit: Portrait of Ivan Kotliarevsky, attributed to Leontiy Kashtelyanchuk (date unknown) · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Ivan Petrovych Kotliarevsky (1769–1838) was born in Poltava, in the Cossack Hetmanate, and was educated at the Poltava seminary. He worked as a tutor and served as an army officer in the Russo-Turkish war of 1806–1812 before directing a charitable institution in his native city, and he was active in the Poltava theatre.

His Eneida, a travesty of Virgil's Aeneid in which the Trojans become Cossacks, first appeared in print in 1798 and is regarded as the first major work written in the vernacular Ukrainian language, and so as the beginning of modern Ukrainian literature. He also wrote the plays Natalka Poltavka and Moskal-Charivnyk.
